title: Neutralisation Reactions
content:
# Neutralisation Reactions

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Define neutralisation and write equations for neutralisation reactions
- Explain what happens in terms of H⁺ and OH⁻ ions
- Give examples of neutralisation in everyday life
- Identify that neutralisation is exothermic

## Introduction

**Neutralisation** is the reaction between an acid and a base. It is one of the most important reactions in chemistry, with applications from cooking and cleaning to medicine and agriculture.

## Key Concepts

### What is Neutralisation?

**Neutralisation:** The reaction between an acid and a base to form a salt and water.

**General equation:**
$$\text{Acid} + \text{Base} \rightarrow \text{Salt} + \text{Water}$$

**Examples:**
$$\text{HCl} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{2KOH} \rightarrow \text{K}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{2H}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{HNO}_3 + \text{Ca(OH)}_2 \rightarrow \text{Ca(NO}_3\text{)}_2 + \text{2H}_2\text{O}$$

### The Ionic Equation

The key reaction in neutralisation is between H⁺ and OH⁻ ions:

$$\text{H}^+\text{(aq)} + \text{OH}^-\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O(l)}$$

This is the same for ALL acid-alkali neutralisations.

**The other ions (Na⁺, Cl⁻, etc.) are spectator ions** - they don't change.

### Energy Change in Neutralisation

Neutralisation is always **exothermic**.

$$\text{H}^+ + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O} \quad \Delta H = -57 \text{ kJ/mol}$$

- Heat is released
- Temperature increases
- Strong acid + strong alkali releases about 57 kJ per mole of water formed

### Types of Neutralisation

**1. Acid + Alkali**
$$\text{HCl(aq)} + \text{NaOH(aq)} \rightarrow \text{NaCl(aq)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)}$$

**2. Acid + Metal oxide (insoluble base)**
$$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\text{(aq)} + \text{CuO(s)} \rightarrow \text{CuSO}_4\text{(aq)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)}$$

**3. Acid + Metal hydroxide (insoluble base)**
$$\text{2HCl(aq)} + \text{Mg(OH)}_2\text{(s)} \rightarrow \text{MgCl}_2\text{(aq)} + \text{2H}_2\text{O(l)}$$

### Naming the Salt

| Acid | Anion | Salt name |
|------|-------|----------|
| Hydrochloric acid (HCl) | Cl⁻ | ...chloride |
| Sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄) | SO₄²⁻ | ...sulfate |
| Nitric acid (HNO₃) | NO₃⁻ | ...nitrate |

The metal comes from the base:

| Base | Salt from HCl | Salt from H₂SO₄ | Salt from HNO₃ |
|------|---------------|-----------------|----------------|
| NaOH | NaCl | Na₂SO₄ | NaNO₃ |
| KOH | KCl | K₂SO₄ | KNO₃ |
| Ca(OH)₂ | CaCl₂ | CaSO₄ | Ca(NO₃)₂ |
| CuO | CuCl₂ | CuSO₄ | Cu(NO₃)₂ |

### Everyday Applications

**Treating acid indigestion:**
- Stomach contains HCl
- Antacids contain bases (Mg(OH)₂, CaCO₃, NaHCO₃)
- They neutralise excess stomach acid
$$\text{Mg(OH)}_2 + \text{2HCl} \rightarrow \text{MgCl}_2 + \text{2H}_2\text{O}$$

**Treating acidic soil:**
- Acidic soil is bad for many crops
- Lime (calcium oxide or calcium hydroxide) is added
- Neutralises the acid
$$\text{CaO} + \text{Acid in soil} \rightarrow \text{Salt} + \text{Water}$$

**Treating bee stings:**
- Bee venom is acidic
- Baking soda (NaHCO₃, a base) can help
- Neutralises the acid

**Treating wasp stings:**
- Wasp venom is alkaline
- Vinegar (ethanoic acid) can help
- Neutralises the alkali

**Treating acid spills:**
- Bases are used to neutralise acid spills
- Makes them safe to clean up

## Worked Examples

**Example 1:** Write the equation for the neutralisation of nitric acid with potassium hydroxide. Name the salt formed.

**Solution:**
$$\text{HNO}_3 + \text{KOH} \rightarrow \text{KNO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

The salt is **potassium nitrate**.

---

**Example 2:** Write the equation for the reaction of sulfuric acid with copper oxide. Include state symbols.

**Solution:**
$$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\text{(aq)} + \text{CuO(s)} \rightarrow \text{CuSO}_4\text{(aq)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)}$$

- Copper oxide is a solid (insoluble base)
- The blue solution formed contains copper sulfate

---

**Example 3:** Write the ionic equation for the neutralisation of any acid by any alkali.

**Solution:**
$$\text{H}^+\text{(aq)} + \text{OH}^-\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O(l)}$$

This is the same for all acid-alkali neutralisations because:
- Acids provide H⁺ ions
- Alkalis provide OH⁻ ions
- These combine to form water
- The other ions are spectators

---

**Example 4:** Explain why farmers add lime (calcium oxide) to acidic soil.

**Solution:**
- Many crops do not grow well in acidic soil
- Calcium oxide is a base
- It reacts with and neutralises the acid in the soil
- CaO + H⁺ → Ca²⁺ + H₂O
- The pH of the soil increases
- This allows crops to grow better

## Common Mistakes

- **Mistake:** Thinking neutralisation always gives pH 7
- **Correct:** Complete neutralisation of strong acid + strong alkali gives pH 7, but weak acids/bases may differ

- **Mistake:** Forgetting water is always a product
- **Correct:** Neutralisation ALWAYS produces salt AND water

- **Mistake:** Writing wrong formula for salt (e.g., NaSO₄ instead of Na₂SO₄)
- **Correct:** Check charges balance - Na⁺ and SO₄²⁻ need ratio 2:1

## Practice Questions

1. Write the general word equation for neutralisation. (1 mark)

2. Write balanced equations for:
   a) Hydrochloric acid + sodium hydroxide (2 marks)
   b) Sulfuric acid + potassium hydroxide (2 marks)
   c) Nitric acid + calcium hydroxide (2 marks)

3. Write the ionic equation for neutralisation and explain why it is the same for all acid-alkali reactions. (3 marks)

4. Explain why neutralisation reactions are exothermic. (2 marks)

5. A student has indigestion (too much stomach acid). Suggest a compound that could help and explain how it works. (3 marks)

6. Write the equation for the reaction of hydrochloric acid with copper oxide. Describe what you would observe during this reaction. (4 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Neutralisation | The reaction between an acid and a base to form a salt and water |
| Salt | An ionic compound formed when an acid reacts with a base |
| Spectator ions | Ions that don't change during a reaction |
| Ionic equation | An equation showing only the ions that change |
| Exothermic | A reaction that releases heat |

## Summary

- **Neutralisation:** Acid + Base → Salt + Water
- **Ionic equation:** H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O (same for all)
- Always **exothermic** (ΔH ≈ -57 kJ/mol)
- **Salt naming:**
  - Metal from the base
  - Anion from the acid (-chloride, -sulfate, -nitrate)
- **Applications:** Antacids, treating soil, treating stings, cleaning acid spills
